subject: Re: Order Form - commercial items to triage (min commit split, net terms, tax evidence)
messages:
From: Alex Jensen <alex@nimbleapps.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@nimbleapps.com>
Date: 2028-06-25T09:12:00Z
Subject: Order Form questions + VAT certificate attached

Hi Kimberly —

Thanks for sending the updated Order Form. We reviewed the redlines and have three blockers from our side before legal signs off:

1) Minimum commit split: We need the contract to allow spreading the annual committed spend across two entities (UK entity + EU hub). Can Redwood accept split invoicing by entity?
2) Net terms: Our AP team requires net 60 for the primary entity but we can do net 30 for the secondary. Is partial net-term mapping something you can support?
3) VAT evidence: I’ve attached our VAT certificate (VAT_certificate_Nimble.pdf). Please confirm whether Redwood needs a separate tax residency form or if this is sufficient.

I’ve attached a marked-up Order Form (Nimble_OrderForm_v3_redlines.pdf) and a proposed payment schedule (proposed_payment_schedule.xlsx). Happy to hop on a quick call if easier.

Thanks,
Alex Jensen
Head of Platform Partnerships
NimbleApps
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Jensen <alex@nimbleapps.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-25T12:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Order Form questions + VAT certificate attached

Alex —

Appreciate the clear summary and the attachments. Looping in Ben (commercial lead) and Karthik (sales engineer) so we can triage internally. Quick reads from our side:

- Split invoicing by entity: This is possible but requires us to capture separate billing entities on the Order Form and route invoices to distinct AP contacts. Finance will want an entity-level commitment and a legal cross-guaranty for the aggregated SLA/commit.
- Mixed net terms: We can support mixed net terms per invoice recipient, but that triggers a credit holdback process and a separate ACH/Wire routing configuration. That usually requires Finance approval for the deal.
- VAT evidence: The attached VAT certificate looks valid; we typically additionally request a signed W-8/B-residency form for auditing if the flow includes cross-border withholding.

Next steps from Redwood:
1) Ben — can you confirm whether we can accept entity-split as structured in the redlines and whether Sales is comfortable with a cross-guarantee clause?
2) Karthik — please review whether the runtime routing or region pinning changes based on entity mapping (this impacts billing SKU alignment).
3) Alex — can you confirm the AP contact details for each entity and whether Nimble will accept a joint invoice for consolidated reporting if requested?

I’ll also pull legal (cc’d separately to lauren) to review the proposed cross-guarantee language.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-26T08:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Order Form questions + VAT certificate attached

Thanks — tagging Lauren from Legal for the cross-guarantee language. Notes from Commercial:

- Entity split: We can do it but need the following captured before countersignature:
  • Entity A (UK) — primary commitment 75% of annual committed spend, billed monthly, net 60.
  • Entity B (NL) — secondary 25% billed quarterly, net 30.
  • A short cross-guarantee paragraph that binds the parent to cover any unpaid amounts up to the full committed value.
- Pricing: No price uplift for split invoicing, but SKUs must map to the same rate table; deviations need approval.
- Escalation: If Collections flags discrepancy > 7 days, Redwood can suspend new provisioning for the affected entity only.

Lauren — can Legal draft a one-paragraph cross-guarantee that is limited in scope (payment-only, no liability for indemnities) and attach to the Order Form as Appendix A? Also confirm whether the net-term split adds any compliance flags.

Karthik — if entity-level routing requires separate model pins (e.g., EU-hosted model variants), we need to capture that in the service appendix; please advise.

-ben
Ben Carter
VP, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-27T16:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Order Form questions + VAT certificate attached

All —

I drafted a narrow payment cross-guarantee that we can insert as Appendix A. Key points:

• Limited scope: guarantees payment obligations under the Order Form only; no additional indemnities or warranty extensions.
• Duration: aligns with the term in the Order Form; terminates once all payment obligations are fully satisfied.
• Caps: guarantee amount = total committed spend in Order Form.
• Governing law: keep as stated in MSA (Delaware) but allow enforcement in competent courts for each billing entity.

Compliance note: Mixed net terms are acceptable operationally, but Finance asks for a short escalation flow in the Order Form (if any invoice is >45 days overdue for entity with net 30, Collections will open a joint reconciliation and reserve right to suspend). That mitigates exposure.

I’ve attached the proposed paragraph inline below and can push a redlined Order Form PDF if you want to review markup.

-- Proposed Appendix A (payment cross-guarantee) --

"The Parent Entity hereby irrevocably guarantees the prompt payment of all amounts due by its Affiliates under this Order Form. This guarantee is limited to payment obligations and shall terminate upon full satisfaction of such obligations. Except as expressly set forth herein, the Parent Entity shall not assume any other obligations or liabilities under the MSA or Order Form."

If that language works for Nimble, I’ll produce a redline of the Order Form and a short schedule that maps invoice recipients to net terms and AP contacts.

Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
